title: Graph DFS: iterative reachability
summary: Every node reachable from start, using an explicit stack instead of recursion. A node is marked when popped, so it may be pushed twice; BFS marks on enqueue instead. O(V + E).
code: # Track visited nodes so cycles cannot cause an infinite traversal.
triggers: reachability or connected components: can A reach B, how many groups
follow one branch to the end before backing up: cycles, ordering, flood fill
prompts: Installing one package pulls in its dependencies, and theirs in turn. List every package that installing a given one brings along.
Rooms are linked by one-way doors. Starting in the lobby, which rooms can a visitor ever reach?
invariant: visited holds exactly the expanded nodes, and every node on the stack is reachable from start.
mantra: Pop, skip if seen, mark, push the unseen neighbours.
pitfalls: Marking on pop allows duplicates on the stack, so the 'if node in visited: continue' guard is required.
Recursive DFS is shorter, but Python's default recursion limit is about 1000 frames.
Cycle detection in a directed graph needs three states: unvisited, on the current path, done.
